studies.title: Better Than A Thousand Months
studies.meaning: The pronoun in the first line has no antecedent in the surah, and the commentators agree it refers to the Quran, sent down on a night the surah names but does not date. Then the question form, which the Quran uses to say that a thing exceeds description. The comparison given is arithmetic and strange: better than a thousand months. Angels descend with every command, and the night is called peace until dawn rather than said to contain peace.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan by the tradition this collection follows, though some authorities place it in Medina. No specific occasion is reported. The night it describes is connected in other passages to the month of fasting, and the sources record several views about which night of that month is meant, generally pointing at the last ten and at the odd-numbered ones, without settling on a date.

keyTerms.note: The root covers determining an amount, having power, and being of value. All three readings are recorded: the night on which things are apportioned, the night of power, and the night of great worth.
A form implying descent in stages or repeatedly rather than in one movement. Used with a present-tense verb, it describes the night as something that happens rather than something that happened once.

The word for peace is placed first and the night second, so the sentence identifies the night with peace rather than describing it as peaceful. Arabic word order carries the emphasis the English has to spell out.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A thousand months is about eighty-three years, which was more than a full lifetime in seventh-century Arabia. The comparison is not an abstraction: it offers a person more than his whole life in the space of one night. For an audience that measured wealth in seasons and life in a few decades, that is the largest exchange rate anyone had heard proposed.
studies.didYouKnow: The phrase naming the night occurs three times in five short lines, which in a surah this length is an unusual density. Nothing else in the chapter is repeated. The effect is that the name arrives, is questioned, and is answered, and by the fourth ayah the surah can stop naming it and simply say what happens in it.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Time is described as unequal, which is a specific claim. One night is said to carry more than eighty years, so the value of a period is not a function of its length. That has a consequence for how a person thinks about a life: what is decisive may occupy very little of it. The night is also left undated, which keeps the search open and makes the last third of a month a period of attention rather than a single appointment.

crossReferences.why: Names the month this night belongs to, and connects the descent of the Quran to the same period.
Describes the same night with a different phrase, adding that every decided matter is separated out in it.
Contains the lines that came down on the night this surah describes, according to the classical accounts.

studies.applyIt: Give one night this year the shape this surah describes: no screen, no plans, a few hours awake with something worth saying. It does not have to be the right night, and nobody knows which that is. The practice the surah produces is looking for it, and looking has to be done on ordinary nights.
